key_headlines.title: Korea's Export Surges 3.687 Trillion Dollars in One Year, 74% Driven by Semiconductors
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's annual exports are on track to reach a historic 1 trillion dollars, with semiconductor exports nearly tripling from 139.2 billion to 413.4 billion dollars year-over-year, driven by the global AI investment boom.

key_headlines.title: Robot Core Components Achieving 80% Localization Rate with Government R&D Support
key_headlines.summary: The government plans to commercialize robot actuators by 2029 and humanoid batteries by 2030 through new initiatives, investing 49.8 billion won in on-sensor AI technology development.

key_headlines.title: Deputy PM Lee Announces 2027 Economic Growth Strategy Focused on Raising Potential Growth and Reducing Polarization
key_headlines.summary: The government will increase economic forecasts from twice to three times annually for the first time in 32 years and will establish a dedicated task force to address wealth polarization.

key_headlines.title: South Korea's Digital and AI Competitiveness Ranks 10th Globally, Rising 8 Positions in One Year
key_headlines.summary: Korea maintains the world's top position in R&D spending as a percentage of GDP and ranks 8th in AI paper indices, with significant improvements in venture capital accessibility and efficiency rankings.

key_headlines.title: Stock Market Settlement Cycle to Transition from T+2 to T+1 with Over Six-Month Testing Period
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's domestic stock settlement system will shift to T+1 after extensive testing and discussions with global investors to address concerns about operational burden and settlement failure protocols.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's exports have surged 3.687 trillion dollars in the past year, approaching a historic 1 trillion dollar annual milestone, with semiconductors accounting for 74.3% of the total export growth. This remarkable increase is driven by the global artificial intelligence investment boom and the semiconductor supercycle. The government is also prioritizing the localization of robot core components to achieve an 80% domestic production rate, with plans to commercialize key components like actuators and humanoid batteries by 2029-2030. Additionally, the Deputy Prime Minister announced that the government's economic growth strategy for 2027 will focus on raising potential growth rates and reducing wealth polarization, with plans to increase economic forecasts from two to three times annually.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The government's 2027 economic strategy will expand economic forecasts to three times per year for the first time in 32 years, enabling faster responses to changing domestic and international conditions. Deputy Prime Minister Lee emphasized that reducing polarization and raising potential growth rates are the two pillars of economic policy going forward. Despite strong semiconductor tax revenues, South Korea faces rising interest costs on temporary borrowing from the central bank, with interest expenses expected to double to 210.5 billion won in 2027 as borrowing rates increase to 3.16%. The U.S. Federal Reserve's potential for a 50 basis point rate hike in December creates uncertainty, while South Korea's fiscal position remains relatively healthy with government debt at 50% of GDP and continued budget deficits below 2% of GDP.
sections.Financial Markets: South Korea's stock market faced pressure from sustained foreign investor selling, though there are proposals to stabilize equities through public fund accumulation of domestic stocks financed by semiconductor sector windfall revenues. The Korean won attempted to re-enter the 1,340 won-to-dollar range as markets monitored Federal Reserve policy decisions, with AI-related stocks rebounding despite concerns about Nvidia's near-term weakness. The KOSPI opened slightly higher at 5,385.94 before consolidating, while the KOSDAQ declined slightly to 698.61. Domestic ETFs focusing on balanced U.S. Nasdaq and domestic bond allocations have gained investor interest amid market volatility, with one product exceeding 500 billion won in net assets.
sections.Industry & Technology: Samsung announced an additional 4 trillion won in Chungcheong region investments, bringing total investments to 144 trillion won, with expansion plans across AI chips, OLED displays, and advanced battery production facilities in Asan, Cheonan, and Sejong. President Lee highlighted that 112 companies across semiconductors, biotechnology, and related sectors have committed to additional investments of 23.6 trillion won in the Chungcheong megaproject zone. The government is actively supporting semiconductor and biotechnology development as key pillars of industrial competitiveness and economic growth. LG CNS held a robotics and physical AI forum bringing together academic and industry experts to explore practical applications of robotics and AI technologies in industrial settings.
sections.Real Estate: South Korea's real estate market shows signs of weakness, with major new apartment complexes near Samsung's Pyeongtaek campus experiencing significant subscription shortfalls despite expected strong demand. Seoul's real estate inventory has accumulated amid economic uncertainty and high interest rates, though certain areas continue to record price increases. The Seoul city government approved development plans for the former CBS broadcast headquarters in Mokdong, transforming it into senior housing and commercial facilities after 34 years of broadcast operations. GS Construction launched a new apartment complex offering 984 units in Ansan, with subscriptions scheduled through November 25.
sections.International Economy: Global export growth is heavily concentrated in AI-related products, with approximately 80% of worldwide export increases attributable to artificial intelligence equipment, creating vulnerability if the AI investment boom subsides. The U.S. Federal Reserve faces inflationary pressures, with inflation rising 0.4% and potential rate hikes of 50 basis points in December, which could impact global financial markets and growth prospects. Korea-U.S. relations are strengthening with semiconductor and shipbuilding serving as leverage points, while Korean-American Congressman-elect Dan Goh criticized potential tariff imposition on allied nations. Historical precedent from 2000-2002 shows that previous IT bubbles resulted in sharp downturns affecting Asian economies, raising concerns about current AI sector concentration risks.
sections.AI & Economy: South Korea's government is poised to exceed 2 trillion won in AI and ICT R&D budgeting for the first time, reinforcing its position as a global R&D powerhouse with R&D investment exceeding 5% of GDP. AI productivity gains generate multiplier effects across industries through external economic benefits, with potential returns exceeding investment multiples and providing long-term GDP growth benefits beyond immediate periods. Naver achieved record quarterly revenue of 3.472 trillion won for the seventh consecutive period and announced plans to invest nearly 1 trillion won in logistics infrastructure by 2030 while securing 2 trillion won in AI factory supply contracts. Meta announced leadership changes in AI and data center infrastructure following massive capital investments, with Santosha Janardan stepping down after 17 years and AWS executive Niv Brown taking over.
sections.Others: Naver reported record third-quarter revenue of 3.472 trillion won driven by commerce, financial platforms, and global C2C transaction growth, alongside plans for major logistics subsidiary investments to enhance delivery competitiveness against Coupang. Korea ranks 10th globally in digital and AI competitiveness, climbing 8 positions in one year, with world-leading R&D spending relative to GDP and improved venture capital accessibility and efficiency rankings. LG CNS hosted a robotics and physical AI forum with leading universities and industry experts to discuss emerging technologies and real-world industrial applications of advanced robotics and machine learning. South Korea has established itself as a competitive force in digital transformation and artificial intelligence, supported by robust government R&D investment and strategic corporate initiatives across major technology conglomerates.
